title: WorksBuddy - Local Document AI Pipeline
subtitle: Production-Grade Local Document Intelligence & OCR Pipeline
summary: Built a scalable local Document Intelligence pipeline for LBM Solution Pvt. Ltd., automating data extraction from invoices, resumes, and visiting cards using FastAPI, PaddleOCR, and local Ollama LLMs (Llama 3.2 / Phi-3) with Pydantic validations.

caseStudy.problem: Manual document data entry is highly labor-intensive and poses severe privacy and data residency compliance risks when using commercial APIs.
caseStudy.research: Compared PaddleOCR, Tesseract, and EasyOCR, selecting PaddleOCR for superior speed and table parsing.
caseStudy.architecture: Asynchronous FastAPI microservice piping image/PDF inputs to PaddleOCR layout analyzers, feeding text blocks to a locally hosted Ollama LLM, and validating structured models via Pydantic.
caseStudy.challenges: Ensuring output schema consistency and preventing model hallucinations under tight CPU/GPU memory constraints.
caseStudy.solutions: Designed specialized system prompts with strict context boundaries and built an automated feedback loop that re-runs structured corrections upon validation errors.
caseStudy.performance: Successfully processed multi-page documents under 1.5 seconds per page with a 99.2% schema compliance rate, eliminating external API fees.
caseStudy.lessonsLearned: Local open-source LLMs combined with structural validators (Pydantic) are fully capable of enterprise-grade entity extraction.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Q&A System (RAG)
subtitle: Multi-Document Q&A Pipeline with Agentic Re-Querying
summary: Developed an end-to-end RAG pipeline using LangChain, FAISS, and OpenAI/HuggingFace embeddings. Features an integrated CrewAI/LangGraph agent that detects low retrieval confidence and triggers dynamic query expansion.

caseStudy.problem: Traditional semantic search often suffers from low precision or returns irrelevant context due to vocabulary mismatch and poor document chunking.
caseStudy.research: Evaluated document splitters, embedding dimensions, and top-k retrieval bounds, arriving at recursive character splitting with a chunk overlap of 200 tokens.
caseStudy.architecture: FastAPI backend exposing retrieval endpoints mapped to a localized FAISS vector store, orchestrating query correction via LangGraph agents.
caseStudy.challenges: Handling ambiguous queries or out-of-distribution questions without serving wrong or hallucinated responses.
caseStudy.solutions: Implemented a LangGraph supervisor agent that analyzes initial similarity search scores. If confidence falls below 0.75, it spawns a CrewAI search worker to expand the query terms.
caseStudy.performance: Maintained retrieval latency under 120ms while resolving 97% of low-confidence queries cleanly.
caseStudy.lessonsLearned: Using agentic fallback systems is highly effective at boosting RAG retrieval precision and user satisfaction.

title: Laptop Price Prediction
subtitle: Supervised Machine Learning Regression & Feature Engineering Model
summary: Built a supervised regression model predicting laptop prices from hardware configurations. Performed exploratory data analysis, target encoding, log transformations, and hyperparameter tuning using Scikit-Learn.

caseStudy.problem: Categorical attributes and manufacturer pricing strategies introduce heavy non-linearity into raw market prices, making simple regressions inaccurate.
caseStudy.research: Conducted thorough EDA to identify price skewness and applied log scaling on the target variable to achieve a normal distribution.
caseStudy.architecture: A clean pipeline in Jupyter executing dataset cleansing, target-encoding brand categorical fields, and scaling numeric metrics.
caseStudy.challenges: Controlling overfitting on high-cardinality columns like processor model numbers.
caseStudy.solutions: Optimized models using Grid Search on Random Forest Regressors, comparing results against Linear and Decision Tree baselines.
caseStudy.performance: The tuned Random Forest model achieved an 89.5% R2 score with a mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) under 8%.
caseStudy.lessonsLearned: Rigorous data preprocessing and categorical feature engineering are the most critical factors for tabular model performance.
